Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Sells
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 03/02/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 142 as introduced could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

Committee: Constitution, Campaigns and Elections
Sponsor: Nordgren
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 03/12/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 500 as introduced proposes a Constitutional Amendment which, if ratified, would authorize the Legislature to call itself into a special session. This constitutional amendment will increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from the State General Fund, by an estimated $100,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2023.
Further, this constitutional amendment could increase the obligations of the Legislature by an estimated $360,000 for each special session called by the Legislature.
Bob Fincher, Chair
Constitution, Campaigns and Elections

Committee: Finance and Taxation Education
Sponsor: Roberts
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 02/03/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 98 as introduced and as amended and reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would enact the Alabama Taxpayer Stimulus Freedom Act of 2021 to exempt from state income and/or financial institution excise taxes the various stimulus payments, advance refunds, grants, and small business loans forgiven due to the coronavirus relief bills passed by Congress.
The bill would also enact the Alabama Business Tax Competitiveness Act to change how business income is apportioned to Alabama, clarify the deduction for business interest expenses, decouple from provisions of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, and allow pass-through entities to elect to be taxed at the entity level.
This bill will increase income tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $12.95 million for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2021, and by an estimated $12.75 million for each fiscal year thereafter.
Arthur Orr, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation Education

Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Simpson
Analyst: Robin Rawls
Date: 02/25/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 52 as passed the House of Representatives provides for the continuance of the Board of Examiners of Nursing Home Administrators until October 1, 2025 pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
